questions.question: A load that is 10 feet long must be secured with at least ____ tie-down(s).
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: Which item is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel as hard as possible

questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes if hydroplaning. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This slows the vehicle and helps it regain traction.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should not move more than:
questions.explanation: Check slack adjusters on level ground with the parking brake off. Pull them to ensure they move no more than one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: During a trip, which valves should be open?
questions.explanation: All shut-off valves must be open during a trip, except for the last valves on the rear trailer. This ensures air reaches all brakes and does not escape from the back.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear, then use brakes to help slow the engine

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear, then use brakes to help slow the engine
questions.explanation: Use the engine's braking power to control speed on downhills. Shift to a lower gear before starting down. Use the brakes only when needed for extra slowing or stopping.

questions.question: How do you test if a tractor protection valve works?

options.text: Release air with the brake pedal and wait for the emergency signal

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air with the brake pedal and wait for the emergency signal
questions.explanation: Test the valve by letting the air supply charge fully, turning off the engine, then pressing the brake pedal several times. The valve should move to emergency mode when air pressure drops too low.

questions.question: When using ABS brakes, how should you brake?

options.text: Brake harder than with other systems

questions.explanation: With Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would with any other braking system.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum weight the manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh
The maximum weight a single vehicle can pull
The minimum weight a single vehicle can haul
The maximum weight allowed on a single trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum weight the manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh
questions.explanation: GVWR is the maximum weight set by the manufacturer for a vehicle and its load combined.

questions.question: Why should you cover cargo?

options.text: To protect the cargo from thieves
To protect the cargo from weather
To prevent other drivers from seeing it

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the cargo from weather
questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights when driving in fog. High beam lights will reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When should an air supply control lever be in its normal position?

options.text: When applying the trailer emergency brakes.

questions.explanation: The air supply control lever should be in its normal position when pulling a trailer. This is the correct setting for tractor protection controls.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Speed up and slow down frequently.
Change your speed and following distance to match the road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed and following distance to match the road conditions.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, adjust your speed and increase your following distance. Your vehicle will need more time to stop. Avoid frequent speed changes.

questions.question: A pre-trip vehicle inspection:

options.text: Is not required if you use the vehicle regularly.
Is not required for trips under 100 miles.
Can only be done by a mechanic.

questions.explanation: State and federal law require drivers to inspect their vehicles before driving.

questions.question: What happens if an engine has no oil?

options.text: The vehicle will use less gas.
The engine can be destroyed quickly.
The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be destroyed quickly.
questions.explanation: An engine needs oil to work. Running an engine without oil will destroy it rapidly.

questions.question: When a vehicle with multiple trailers turns, do the rearmost wheels follow a different path than the front wheels?
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking.

questions.question: What should you know about the radiator cap?

options.text: Do not remove it when the coolant is hot.
You can remove it when the coolant is hot.
It should be cool to touch during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not remove it when the coolant is hot.
questions.explanation: Never remove the radiator cap while the system is hot. Hot steam and water can escape and cause severe burns. If the cap is cool to touch, the system is safe to open.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed to secure a 10-foot piece of cargo?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks.
Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
Activates the emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Keeps the spring brakes in place until they are needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It prevents air from escaping the system if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: How can you help your vehicle be seen by others?

options.text: Turn off headlights during the day.
Use headlights only when it rains.

questions.explanation: Clean headlights provide more light at night. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.
